BXL-2425-00008-v13.headline: Cut the budget allocated to Brussels ministers' personal staffs (cabinets) by 20% in the regional provisional credits for 2025, locking in the savings the caretaker government only set by internal circular.
BXL-2425-00008-v13.proposed_by: Benjamin Dalle and Christophe De Beukelaer (cd&v)
BXL-2425-00008-v13.source_brief:
Brussels ministerial cabinets — the large personal political staffs each minister is entitled to — are, by several accounts cited in debate, the biggest in Belgium relative to the region's size. A caretaker government circular already ordered 50% savings internally over summer 2024, but that circular has no legal force. This amendment would have hardwired a 20% cut into the provisional 2025 budget ordinance itself, binding any incoming government from day one.

- **What it actually changes in numbers.** The personnel spending line for ministerial cabinets (mission 34, programme 001) would drop from 10.347 to 6.208 thousand euros in the provisional credits — roughly a 40% cut on that specific allocation, calibrated to represent three months at 80% of the annual envelope.
- **Supporters say** the Brussels Region's cabinet budgets have ballooned by about 50% since 2020 — from roughly €21M to €31M a year — and Parliament can and should signal a ceiling before a new government is formed.
- **Opponents argue** the timing is wrong: a new government forming in January or February 2025 would need to staff up its cabinets immediately, and locking in a percentage cut via provisional credits does not respect the legal obligations employers have to existing staff, such as severance pay.
- **The rub:** whether Parliament should pre-empt a government-formation deal on cabinet size by writing it into a stopgap budget, or whether this kind of structural decision should wait for a full budget with proper debate.
deep_facts: Amendment no. 1 to article 6 (tableau budgétaire / begrotingstabel) of A-47, the finance ordinance opening provisional credits for January-March 2025 on the Brussels-Capital regional budget; the amendment modifies mission 34, programme 001 (CRI, 19 Dec 2024).

The specific change proposed: allocation de base 34.001.04 (Dépenses de personnel / Personeelsuitgaven) reduced from 10.347 thousand euros to 6.208 thousand euros in both liquidation and engagement credits; the totals for programme 001 adjusted accordingly from 10.834 to 6.695 thousand euros; totals for mission 34 adjusted from 79.834 to 75.695 thousand euros (CRI, 19 Dec 2024).

The movers' stated rationale: the provisional-twelfths mechanism should carry forward the 2024 budget, including decisions taken in 2024; the caretaker government had decided in summer 2024 to reduce cabinet spending by 50% and issued a circular to that effect; the amendment proposes 20% (not 50%) to leave a margin for wage indexations, possible redundancy payments and the start-up needs of a new government (CRI, 19 Dec 2024).

Figures cited on cabinet credit growth: Brussels ministerial cabinet budgets grew from just over 21 million euros in 2020 to just over 31 million euros at the time of debate — an increase of approximately 50%, described as far exceeding inflation; the amendment was framed as saving approximately 6 million euros per year (CRI, 19 Dec 2024).

Brussels ministerial cabinets were described in debate as the largest in Belgium; the federal government, responsible for all Belgians, and the Flemish government, responsible for 6.5 million people, were said to operate with smaller cabinet staffs than those of the Brussels-Capital Region (CRI, 19 Dec 2024).

The caretaker government had already issued a circular (rondzendbrieven / circulaire) over summer 2024 requiring 50% savings on cabinet credits; Minister-President Vervoort confirmed the circular made new hiring impossible, but noted the next government was not bound by it (CRI, 19 Dec 2024).

The government opposed the amendment: a spokesperson for the majority noted that cabinets, like any employer, have financial obligations — wage indexations, contractual engagements, possible termination indemnities — making a fixed percentage cut by Parliament premature at this stage; the appropriate moment was said to be a full budget debate or government-formation negotiations (CRI, 19 Dec 2024).

N-VA stated support: the Brussels cabinets are too large compared to other regions and should be reduced; whether via the amendment or via formation negotiations was said to be secondary (CRI, 19 Dec 2024).

PTB abstained: the group said it favours smaller cabinets, especially as Brussels cabinets are the largest in the country while the Region is not the largest, but objected to wording in the explanatory note that could be read as requiring automatic savings across all entities (CRI, 19 Dec 2024).

MR (majority) opposed on timing grounds: imposing a fixed reduction now would hamper a full-exercise government forming in January or February 2025 from constituting its cabinets from the start; the debate on cabinet size could be opened in the context of a full budget, but not at this point (CRI, 19 Dec 2024).
BXL-2425-00008-v13.deep_lectura:
**Analyst read** *(inference — not stated verbatim in the record)*

- The amendment's real significance is jurisdictional: by writing a cabinet-size constraint into a legally binding provisional-credits ordinance, opposition groups would pre-empt the formation negotiations still under way — effectively giving Parliament the first move on what is normally an executive prerogative (staffing one's own political teams).
- The choice of 20% rather than 50% reads as a deliberate concession to plausibility: a figure no new government could credibly call unworkable, since the caretaker had already been operating at 50% by circular. The gap between 50% and 20% is the concession to the majority needed to seek cross-aisle support.
- The MR's 'wrong moment' objection is procedurally correct but also self-interested: as the party providing the formateur, MR has every reason to keep cabinet-size decisions off the statute books and inside the formation room, where it controls the outcome.
- The PTB abstention on the wording of the justification note rather than on the substance signals that the party's real concern is coalition arithmetic — a yes vote here would have given the cd&v-led initiative a cross-spectrum stamp of approval it did not yet have.
BXL-2425-00008-v13.raw_fr: Un amendement n° 1, déposé à l'article 6 (tableau budgétaire) de l'ordonnance de finances A-47, propose de réduire de 20 % les crédits alloués aux dépenses de personnel des cabinets ministériels bruxellois dans les crédits provisoires pour janvier-mars 2025, en ramenant l'allocation de base 34.001.04 de 10.347 à 6.208 milliers d'euros. Les auteurs font valoir que les cabinets bruxellois, dont le budget a progressé d'environ 50 % depuis 2020 pour atteindre plus de 31 millions d'euros annuels, sont les plus importants du pays, et que la décision de réduire leurs crédits prise par le gouvernement en affaires courantes devrait être inscrite dans le texte légal. La majorité s'y est opposée, jugeant prématuré d'imposer une réduction forfaitaire avant la formation d'un gouvernement de plein exercice.
